title: Egress resolver UDP multiplexing causing cross-tenant CNAME bleed during peering switchover
creator: Emma Zhou
description:
Summary: Multiple Dedicated customers reported intermittent DNS responses resolving to other tenants' internal hostnames (CNAME chains pointing to private hostnames) during rapid egress gateway failovers and peering route flips. This allows a transient, read-only leakage of hostname resolution results between tenants.

Scope & impact: Affects Dedicated clusters using the shared egress gateway configuration with VPC peering enabled and high outbound DNS churn (large fleets of short-lived containers performing many DNS queries). Customers reported user-facing failures and escalations from 3 enterprise accounts (Acme Analytics, Thermion Health, BrightCart).

Observed behavior: During peering switchover or gateway failover, DNS responses for some tenants briefly included CNAMEs that resolved to private hostnames owned by a different tenant. The application-level symptom varied (service discovery lookups pointing to non-routable internal names, increased 5xxs when backend calls attempted to use leaked names). No data plane payloads besides DNS were observed to cross tenant boundaries.

Why this ticket: Production fix required to prevent recurrence and to provide remediation/rollback guidance for impacted customers while long-term code changes are deployed.
reproduction_steps: Deploy a Dedicated cluster using shared egress gateway and enable VPC peering to a partner VPC
Create two tenants (T-A and T-B) each running thousands of short-lived tasks that each perform DNS queries against external resolvers (high rate of unique hostnames)
Trigger a peering route flap or forcibly failover the egress gateway (simulate node drain/eviction) while churn is ongoing
Observe DNS responses seen by T-A occasionally containing CNAMEs that point to T-B private hostnames
Collect pcap on egress proxy and conntrack snapshots to confirm UDP responses were delivered to the wrong tenant socket after rebinding
root_cause: The immediate root cause is UDP response demultiplexing during fast socket rebinds on the shared egress proxy. We multiplex tenant resolver traffic over a small set of UDP sockets, relying on ephemeral conntrack entries and a short-lived socket mapping table. During peering switchover and egress proxy restarts the mapping table was rebuilt non-deterministically; UDP responses that arrived while mappings were being rebuilt were associated with the wrong tenant due to a race between conntrack expiration and the proxy's per-tenant demux layer. This was exacerbated by: (1) reuse of ephemeral source ports across tenants, (2) aggressive conntrack timeouts tuned for TCP workloads, and (3) no per-tenant tagging of UDP replies at the kernel/netfilter level.
mitigations: Hotfix: enable per-tenant dedicated UDP sockets in the egress proxy config (feature-flag rollout to reduce blast radius)
Operational: during customer escalations, perform graceful node drains of egress gateways instead of hard evictions to allow conntrack to quiesce
Temporary policy: increase conntrack UDP timeout on dedicated clusters to reduce demux races until patch is live
Customer-side workaround: for affected customers, enable local stub resolvers pinned to per-tenant resolver IP (documented step-by-step)
proposed_fix: Code change in egress-proxy: allocate one UDP socket namespace per tenant (or otherwise tag packets with tenant ID before kernel visibility) and avoid port reuse across tenants. Add a deterministic socket->tenant binding that survives transient rebinds. Update conntrack tuning to distinguish tenant flows and add netfilter MARK for tenant tag so replies are routed to correct namespace even under transient route changes. Include unit & integration tests that simulate peering flips and socket rebind races.
rollout_plan: 1) Merge egress-proxy per-tenant-socket patch behind feature flag (infra PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/5821)
2) Canary rollout to 2 low-risk Dedicated clusters with synthetic churn (72h soak)
3) Expand rollout to clusters hosting tier-1 customers over 48h with monitoring and kill-switch
4) For clusters with customer-reported incidents, schedule in-place migration with graceful drain and apply updated conntrack settings
5) Remove feature flag and finalize regression tests in CI
qa_checks: Synthetic churn test that exercises 10k DNS queries/sec across 100 tenants while performing controlled peering switches
Packet-level validation that every DNS response has netfilter MARK matching tenant ID
Automated injection test that simulates egress gateway restart and ensures zero cross-tenant DNS mappings observed
Long-run soak (72h) on canary cluster validated by SRE and product owners
recent_updates: 2026-03-10: Incident opened after Acme Analytics reported DNS drift during scheduled peering maintenance. Escalated to engineering P0.
2026-03-11: Collected pcap and conntrack dumps from affected clusters. Initial hypothesis formed: UDP demux race during socket rebound.
2026-03-12: Built local repro harness that reproduces leak within 3-5 minutes under synthetic churn. First prototype of per-tenant socket binding validated locally.
2026-03-13: Hotfix feature flag implemented; SRE applied temporary conntrack tuning on impacted clusters. No new customer leaks observed after tuning (monitoring continues).
2026-03-14: Code review feedback addressed for infra PR #5821. Preparing canary rollout plan and customer communications.
